_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present -ar
entries.usage: What happens now or regularly, -ar verbs.
entries.example: Yo hablo español.

entries.label: Present -er/-ir
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -er and -ir verbs.
entries.example: Como pan y vivo aquí.

entries.label: Preterite
entries.usage: A finished past action.
entries.example: Ayer hablé con ella.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The ongoing or habitual past.
entries.example: De niño jugaba mucho.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen, one word.
entries.example: Mañana comeré tarde.

entries.label: Conditional
entries.usage: What would happen.
entries.example: Yo viviría en el mar.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: Wishes, doubts, requests after que.
entries.example: Espero que hables pronto.

entries.label: Progressive
entries.usage: Happening right now: estar + -ando/-iendo.
entries.example: Estoy comiendo ahora.

entries.label: Preterite irregulars
entries.usage: The common irregular preterites.
entries.example: Fui al centro y lo hice.

entries.label: Past subjunctive
entries.usage: Hypotheticals and softened requests.
entries.example: Si hablara más, entendería.

entries.label: Ser (identity)
entries.usage: For saying who or what someone is — where they are from, what they do, what they are like.
entries.example: Yo soy estudiante. — I am a student.

entries.point: The verb estar — location and states
entries.label: Estar (location)
entries.usage: For where something is, and for how someone feels at the moment — tired, happy, at home.
entries.example: Yo estoy en casa. — I am at home.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: For saying something is not so — put no directly in front of the verb.
entries.example: No tengo tiempo. — I don't have time.

entries.label: Hay (there is)
entries.usage: For saying something exists or is around — one word covers both there is and there are, and it never changes shape.
entries.example: Hay un libro en la mesa. — There is a book on the table.

entries.label: Reflexives
entries.usage: For things you do to yourself, like getting up or washing — a small word (me, te, se) goes in front of the verb.
entries.example: Yo me levanto a las siete. — I get up at seven.

entries.label: Gustar
entries.usage: For saying you like something: the verb follows the thing liked, so it is me gusta el café but me gustan los libros.
entries.example: Me gusta el café. — I like coffee.

entries.label: Near future
entries.usage: For plans and whatever is about to happen — put voy a, vas a or vamos a in front of the plain verb.
entries.example: Voy a viajar mañana. — I am going to travel tomorrow.

entries.label: Present perfect
entries.usage: For something finished that still counts today — he, has or ha followed by the -ado/-ido form.
entries.example: Hoy he trabajado mucho. — Today I have worked a lot.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: For telling one person to do something, or not to do it — the two are built from different forms.
entries.example: ¡Abre la puerta! — Open the door!

entries.label: Impersonal se
entries.usage: For saying what people do in general, or what gets done, without naming anyone.
entries.example: Se habla español aquí. — Spanish is spoken here.

entries.label: Si-clauses
entries.usage: For if-sentences — one shape for what will happen when it is likely, another for what would happen if it is not.
entries.example: Si estudias, aprobarás. — If you study, you will pass.

entries.label: Pluperfect
entries.usage: For something that had already happened before another moment in the past.
entries.example: Cuando llegué, ya había salido. — When I arrived, she had already left.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: For passing on what someone said earlier, which pushes every verb one step further into the past.
entries.example: Dijo que estaba cansado. — He said he was tired.

entries.label: Para que, aunque
entries.usage: For saying what you do something for, and for granting an even-if you are not sure about.
entries.example: Te lo digo para que lo sepas. — I'm telling you so that you know.

entries.label: Perfect subjunctive
entries.usage: For something already done that you hope for, doubt, or do not believe.
entries.example: Espero que hayas llegado bien. — I hope you have arrived safely.

entries.label: Unreal past (si hubiera)
entries.usage: For looking back at what never happened — if I had studied, I would have passed.
entries.example: Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado. — If I had studied, I would have passed.

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: For formal or written Spanish, where the thing acted on comes first and whoever did it follows por.
entries.example: La novela fue escrita en 1967. — The novel was written in 1967.

entries.label: Emphasis with ser
entries.usage: For pointing at the one part of the sentence that matters — it was María who said it.
entries.example: Fue María quien lo dijo. — It was María who said it.

entries.point: Concessive intensifiers (por más que, digan lo que digan)
entries.label: Por más que
entries.usage: For insisting that nothing will change the outcome — however much you try, whatever they say.
entries.example: Por más que insistas, no lo lograrás. — However much you insist, you won't manage it.

entries.label: Ojalá & -se (literary)
entries.usage: For the -se forms you meet in books, and for wishing out loud for something unlikely with ojalá.
entries.example: Si él supiese la verdad, callaría. — If he knew the truth, he would keep quiet.

entries.label: No es que
entries.usage: For rejecting the reason someone assumed and giving the real one instead.
entries.example: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo. — It's not that I don't want to — it's that I can't.

entries.label: Stem changes
entries.usage: Many everyday verbs swap their middle vowel in the present — quiero, puedo — while the nosotros form keeps the plain one.
entries.example: Yo quiero un café, por favor. — I want a coffee, please.

entries.label: Definite article
entries.usage: el/la/los/las agree with the noun.
entries.example: el libro, la casa

entries.label: Indefinite article
entries.usage: un/una/unos/unas.
entries.example: un coche, una mesa

entries.label: Adjectives
entries.usage: Adjectives match gender and number.
entries.example: un coche rojo, casas rojas

entries.label: Possessives
entries.usage: mi/tu/su and plurals.
entries.example: mis amigos, tu casa

entries.label: Demonstratives
entries.usage: this/that agree with the noun.
entries.example: este día, aquella noche

entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: For saying who is doing something when it is not obvious, or to stress it — most of the time you leave the word out, because the verb ending already says who.
entries.example: Yo soy de México. — I am from Mexico.

entries.label: Gender & number
entries.usage: For picking el or la every time you name a thing, and adding -s or -es when there is more than one — the words around it copy that choice.
entries.example: Tengo dos libros. — I have two books.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: For asking a question that needs a real answer rather than yes or no — qué for a thing, dónde for a place, cómo for the way — with the verb straight after.
entries.example: ¿Dónde estás? — Where are you?

entries.point: Direct object pronouns (lo, la, los, las)
entries.label: Direct objects
entries.usage: For replacing something already mentioned with lo, la, los or las, matching the word it stands for.
entries.example: ¿El libro? Lo tengo yo. — The book? I have it.

entries.label: Indirect objects
entries.usage: For the person something is given, said or sent to — usually named again after a.
entries.example: Le di el libro a Juan. — I gave the book to Juan.

entries.label: Comparatives
entries.usage: For saying one thing is more, less, or just as much as another.
entries.example: Ella es más alta que yo. — She is taller than me.

entries.label: Por vs para
entries.usage: Para looks ahead to who or what something is for; por looks back at the cause, the price, or the way through.
entries.example: Este regalo es para ti. — This gift is for you.

entries.label: Se lo
entries.usage: For when you drop both the thing and the person at once — I gave it to him: the person comes first, and le turns into se in front of lo or la.
entries.example: ¿El libro? Se lo di ayer a Juan. — The book? I gave it to Juan yesterday.

entries.label: Relative pronouns
entries.usage: For adding a with-whom or a whose to the person or thing you are describing.
entries.example: La mujer con quien hablé es doctora. — The woman with whom I spoke is a doctor.

entries.label: Personal a
entries.usage: Put a in front of a particular person you do something to — veo a Juan, but veo la película.
entries.example: Veo a Juan todos los días. — I see Juan every day.
